name: Ducktail haircut

lead: The ducktail is a men's hairstyle in which the sides are greased and combed back to meet at a central ridge at the back of the head, resembling a duck's tail. It gives a retro, 1950s rockabilly or greaser look with a strong head shape from the front and side.
Philadelphia barber Joe Cirello said he invented it in 1940, and it spread in the 1950s with youth subcultures and Elvis Presley.

paras: The cut is grown out on top and sides and styled with pomade or grease, using a fine comb to create a centre part at the back and a pompadour or swept front. Maintenance is regular combing and product.
Heavy pomade can build up on scalp and clothing. Style associations with the greaser subculture are part of its appeal and vary by audience.

lead: The ducktail, also called the duck's ass or DA, is a hairstyle with the hair greased and combed back along the sides to meet in a centre line at the back of the head. People wear it for a vintage, rebellious look associated with 1950s youth culture. [1][2]

Wikipedia reports that Philadelphia barber Joe Cirello said he invented the style in 1940, calling it 'The Swing', and that it became an emblem of disaffected young men across the English-speaking world in the 1950s, helped by Elvis Presley and, in India, Shammi Kapoor. [2] It is linked to greasers and, in Britain, to Teddy Boys and Rockers. [2]
Variants include the Detroit, which combined long back and sides with a flattop, and a California version with a wavy pompadour called a breaker. [2]

paras: Hair is greased, combed back around the sides and parted down the back of the head; the top front is left loose or curled. [2]

Popular in the 1950s, it was used by Hollywood to represent 1950s youth although only a minority of men wore it. [2] Grokipedia ties it to greaser culture, leather jackets and films with James Dean and Marlon Brando. [1]
